```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_rt6h"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0299501>
* Supplement (S1 Table, parameter estimates): <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0299501.s001>

Szederkenyi et al. measured the penetration of topically applied 2% O/W creams
through excised skin mounted in a dynamic "skin-on-a-chip" microfluidic
diffusion chamber, and described every measured cumulative-permeation curve
with the same three-compartment linear ODE model (Section 2.7, Eq 1). The
three compartments are the layers of the skin obtained by spatially
discretising a diffusion-convection equation: a constant zero-order input
`kin` from the cream enters the outermost layer, neighbouring layers exchange
drug by diffusion (`kd`, both directions) and by inward convection (`kc`), and
the deepest layer loses drug at the first-order rate `kout`. The only
observed quantity is the deepest-layer state, `y = x3`, which the authors fit
to the cumulative drug mass permeated into the receptor fluid per cm^2 of
diffusion surface.

The model was fitted separately to each experiment's mean curve, giving 13
independent parameter sets (S1 Table). nlmixr2lib ships each as its own model:

```{r models}
cases <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                                    ~experiment,                                ~figure,  ~tend, ~mass_unit,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_rt6h",          "Caffeine, rat skin, 23.5 C, 6 h",          "4A",     6,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_32c6h",         "Caffeine, rat skin, 32 C, 6 h",            "4B",     6,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_rt12h",         "Caffeine, rat skin, 23.5 C, 12 h",         "5",      12,    "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_dexamethasone",          "Dexamethasone acetate, rat skin",          "6A",     6,     "ng/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_piroxicam",              "Piroxicam, rat skin",                      "6B",     6,     "ng/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_indomethacin",           "Indomethacin, rat skin",                   "6C",     6,     "ng/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_diclofenac",             "Diclofenac, rat skin",                     "6D",     6,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_vaseline24h",   "Caffeine, mouse skin, vaseline 24 h",      "8A",     5,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_vaseline96h",   "Caffeine, mouse skin, vaseline 96 h",      "8B",     5,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_imiquimod24h",  "Caffeine, mouse skin, imiquimod 24 h",     "8C",     5,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_imiquimod96h",  "Caffeine, mouse skin, imiquimod 96 h",     "8D",     5,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_ear_acetone",   "Caffeine, mouse ear, acetone control",     "10A",    5,     "ug/cm^2",
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_ear_tncb",      "Caffeine, mouse ear, TNCB allergic",       "10B",    5,     "ug/cm^2"
)
uis <- lapply(cases$model, function(nm) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm)))
names(uis) <- cases$model
knitr::kable(cases |> dplyr::select(model, experiment, figure))
```

# Population

There is no human or animal population in the usual sense: each model
describes the mean of three replicate skin samples (n = 3 per experiment,
figure captions) in one ex vivo set-up. The chamber has a 0.5 cm^2 diffusion
surface between the cream-filled donor chamber and a receptor chamber perfused
with peripheral perfusion fluid (147 mM NaCl, 4 mM KCl, 2.3 mM CaCl2, pH 7.4)
at 4 uL/min; receptor fluid was collected every 30 or 15 min (Section 2.4).

* Healthy-skin experiments (caffeine at room temperature and at 32 C, and the
  four anti-inflammatory creams) used tape-stripped abdominal skin of rats
  weighing 599-615 g (Sections 2.4 and 2.6).
* Psoriasiform dermatitis was induced in male C57BL/6J mice (21.7-27.0 g) with
  0.0625 g of 5% imiquimod cream on the shaved back (once for the 24 h group,
  daily for the 96 h group), with vaseline-treated time-matched controls
  (Section 2.5).
* Allergic contact dermatitis was induced in male C57BL/6J mice (24.2-31.2 g)
  by sensitising the abdomen with 3% TNCB (controls: acetone) and challenging
  both ears with 1% TNCB on day 5; the ear tissue was mounted in the chamber
  (Section 2.5).

Caffeine was assayed by NanoDrop spectrophotometry at 273 nm and the
anti-inflammatory drugs by LC-MS/MS. The same information is stored in each
model's `population` metadata:

```{r population}
str(uis[["Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_rt6h"]]$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its row of S1
Table. All four parameters were estimated (Matlab `fmincon`, Eq 7) on the
linear scale and are reported without uncertainty; nlmixr2lib stores them
log-transformed.

| Model element | Source location |
|---------------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(skin_slab1)`, `d/dt(skin_slab2)`, `d/dt(skin_slab3)` | Section 2.7, Eq 1 (states `x1`, `x2`, `x3`) |
| Output `cum_mass <- skin_slab3` | Section 2.7 ("The only measured concentration is y = x3"); figure y-axes (cumulative mass per cm^2) |
| `lkin`, `lkdiff`, `lkconv`, `lkout` (paper `kin`, `kd`, `kc`, `kout`) | S1 Table, one row per model |
| Zero initial conditions | Figures 4-10 (all simulated curves start at 0); S1 Table reports no initial-condition estimates |
| Time unit (h) | Figure x-axes |
| Mass units (ug/cm^2 or ng/cm^2) | Figure y-axes; Table 2 |

```{r source-trace-table}
s1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(cases$model, function(nm) {
  th <- uis[[nm]]$theta
  tibble::tibble(
    model = nm,
    kin = exp(th[["lkin"]]),
    kd = exp(th[["lkdiff"]]),
    kc = exp(th[["lkconv"]]),
    kout = exp(th[["lkout"]])
  )
}))
knitr::kable(s1, digits = 6, caption = "Back-transformed parameters (compare S1 Table).")
```

# Simulation

The models carry no between-sample variability and no residual error, so each
is solved once at its typical values. There are no dose records: the cream is
the constant input `kin`.

```{r simulate}
sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cases)), function(i) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(seq(0, cases$tend[i], by = 0.05))
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(uis[[cases$model[i]]], events = ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
  tibble::tibble(
    model = cases$model[i],
    experiment = cases$experiment[i],
    figure = cases$figure[i],
    mass_unit = cases$mass_unit[i],
    time = s$time,
    cum_mass = s$cum_mass
  )
}))
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r plot-helper}
plot_cases <- function(figs, title) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::filter(figure %in% figs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = paste0("Fig ", figure, ": ", experiment, " (", mass_unit, ")")) |>
    ggplot(aes(time, cum_mass)) +
    geom_line(colour = "red") +
    facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cumulative mass permeated per cm^2", title = title)
}
```

plot_cases(c("4A", "4B", "5"), "Caffeine through healthy rat skin") +

```

```

```

```

# Validation

The paper reports no NCA, so PKNCA does not apply. The checks below compare
the packaged models against the printed numbers that the paper does give, and
against the closed-form solution of Eq 1.

## Final cumulative mass against the published curves

The final value of each red simulated curve in Figures 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 was
read off the figure by the maintainers (precision about 2-3% of the axis
range). The packaged models reproduce every one within 5%.

```{r figure-endpoints}
digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~figure, ~fig_end,
  "4A",    37.0,
  "4B",    61.0,
  "5",     101,
  "6A",    830,
  "6B",    1560,
  "6C",    140,
  "6D",    67.5,
  "8A",    8.75,
  "8B",    9.65,
  "8C",    43.3,
  "8D",    35.5,
  "10A",   2.90,
  "10B",   4.08
)
final <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(model, figure, mass_unit) |>
  dplyr::filter(time == max(time)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(model, figure, mass_unit, time, cum_mass) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(digitised, by = "figure") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cum_mass / fig_end - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(final) == nrow(cases), all(abs(final$pct_diff) < 5))
final |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Figure" = figure,
    "Units" = mass_unit,
    "Time (h)" = time,
    "Simulated" = cum_mass,
    "Published (figure)" = fig_end,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

## Table 2 acceptance windows

Table 2 lists the a-posteriori acceptance window for the measured cumulative
mass at the end of each healthy-skin experiment; replicates outside it were
excluded before fitting. A faithful fit to the mean of the accepted
replicates must end inside the window.

```{r table-2}
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                             ~lower, ~upper,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_rt6h",   20,     50,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_32c6h",  40,     75,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_rt12h",  80,     120,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_dexamethasone",   600,    1000,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_indomethacin",    100,    200,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_piroxicam",       1200,   2000,
  "Szederkenyi_2024_diclofenac",      50,     100
)
t2 <- final |>
  dplyr::select(model, mass_unit, cum_mass) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table2, by = "model")
stopifnot(nrow(t2) == 7, all(t2$cum_mass > t2$lower & t2$cum_mass < t2$upper))
knitr::kable(t2, digits = 1)
```

## Disease effects stated in the text

Section 3.5 states that imiquimod raised the caffeine permeability "more than
4 times at 24 h, and more than 3.5 times at 96 h" over the time-matched
vaseline controls; Section 3.6 states that allergic contact dermatitis raised
the ear permeability by 30%.

```{r disease-ratios}
end_of <- function(nm) final$cum_mass[final$model == nm]
ratios <- tibble::tibble(
  comparison = c("Imiquimod / vaseline, 24 h", "Imiquimod / vaseline, 96 h", "TNCB / acetone (ear)"),
  simulated_ratio = c(
    end_of("Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_imiquimod24h") / end_of("Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_vaseline24h"),
    end_of("Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_imiquimod96h") / end_of("Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_vaseline96h"),
    end_of("Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_ear_tncb") / end_of("Szederkenyi_2024_caffeine_ear_acetone")
  ),
  paper = c("> 4", "> 3.5", "1.3")
)
stopifnot(
  ratios$simulated_ratio[1] > 4,
  ratios$simulated_ratio[2] > 3.5,
  ratios$simulated_ratio[3] > 1
)
knitr::kable(ratios, digits = 2)
```

The imiquimod ratios meet the stated thresholds. The ear ratio from the fitted
curves at 5 h is about 1.4 rather than the stated 1.3; the measured curves of
Figure 10 end at about 2.95 and 4.1 ug/cm^2, also a ratio near 1.4, so the
paper's 30% presumably comes from a different summary (for example the
permeation rate over part of the experiment) that is not reported.

## Closed-form solution and the eliminated model (Eqs 2-6)

Eq 1 is linear, `x' = A x + b` with `b = (kin, 0, 0)` and zero initial
state, so `x(t) = A^-1 (exp(A t) - I) b`. The packaged ODE must match this
to integration precision. The authors' identifiability argument rewrites the
model as `y''' + theta1 y'' + theta2 y' + theta3 y + theta4 = 0` (Eqs 2-6);
`theta1..theta3` are the characteristic-polynomial coefficients of `A`, and
the steady state of `y` is `-theta4 / theta3 = kin / kout`. Both identities
are checked for every parameter set.

```{r closed-form}
system_matrix <- function(kd, kc, kout) {
  matrix(c(
    -(kd + kc), kd, 0,
    kd + kc, -(2 * kd + kc), kd,
    0, kd + kc, -(kd + kout)
  ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
}
x3_closed_form <- function(times, kin, kd, kc, kout) {
  A <- system_matrix(kd, kc, kout)
  e <- eigen(A)
  vinv <- solve(e$vectors)
  b <- c(kin, 0, 0)
  vapply(times, function(t) {
    expAt <- Re(e$vectors %*% diag(exp(e$values * t)) %*% vinv)
    (solve(A, (expAt - diag(3)) %*% b))[3]
  }, numeric(1))
}
cf <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(s1)), function(i) {
  p <- s1[i, ]
  s <- sim[sim$model == p$model, ]
  A <- system_matrix(p$kd, p$kc, p$kout)
  minors <- A[1, 1] * A[2, 2] - A[1, 2] * A[2, 1] +
    A[2, 2] * A[3, 3] - A[2, 3] * A[3, 2] +
    A[1, 1] * A[3, 3] - A[1, 3] * A[3, 1]
  theta <- c(
    2 * p$kc + 4 * p$kd + p$kout,
    p$kc^2 + 3 * p$kc * p$kd + 2 * p$kout * p$kc + 3 * p$kd^2 + 3 * p$kout * p$kd,
    p$kout * p$kc^2 + 2 * p$kout * p$kc * p$kd + p$kout * p$kd^2,
    -p$kin * (p$kc + p$kd)^2
  )
  tibble::tibble(
    model = p$model,
    ode_vs_closed_form = max(abs(s$cum_mass - x3_closed_form(s$time, p$kin, p$kd, p$kc, p$kout))) /
      max(s$cum_mass),
    theta_vs_charpoly = max(abs(c(-sum(diag(A)), minors, -det(A)) / theta[1:3] - 1)),
    steady_state = -theta[4] / theta[3],
    steady_state_vs_kin_over_kout = abs(-theta[4] / theta[3] / (p$kin / p$kout) - 1)
  )
}))
# The ODE-vs-closed-form error is integration error at rtol = 1e-10; the
# theta and steady-state identities are pure floating-point algebra.
stopifnot(
  all(cf$ode_vs_closed_form < 1e-6),
  all(cf$theta_vs_charpoly < 1e-10),
  all(cf$steady_state_vs_kin_over_kout < 1e-10)
)
knitr::kable(cf, digits = 12)
```

The steady-state column also shows why most curves in the paper still rise
almost linearly at the end of the experiment: with `kout` as small as 1e-5
1/h, the deepest layer would only level off at `kin / kout`, far beyond the
measured range.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **One model per experiment.** The paper fits the same structure separately
  to each of 13 experiments and reports 13 parameter sets with no shared
  parameters, so nlmixr2lib ships 13 models rather than one model with
  experiment indicators.
- **Compartment names.** The three states `x1..x3` are the layers of a
  spatially discretised diffusion-convection equation and are named with the
  method-of-lines family `skin_slab1..skin_slab3`, numbered from the skin
  surface inward. The slab count of 3 is fixed by the published fit, not a
  numerical choice, so no convergence check applies.
- **Parameter names.** The paper's `kd` (diffusion) and `kc` (convection) are
  stored as `kdiff` and `kconv`, because `kd` is the library's name for a
  dissociation rate constant. `kin` and `kout` keep their names.
- **No variability or residual error.** The authors fitted each mean curve by
  minimising a relative 2-norm (Eq 7) and report no residual-error magnitude,
  so the models carry typical values only and expose the output as the
  algebraic variable `cum_mass` without an error model. The minimum objective
  value `V_min` of each fit is recorded in the model's `population$notes`.
- **Units.** Time is in hours and the states are mass per cm^2 of diffusion
  surface, from the figure axes. The states are called concentrations in
  Section 2.7, but the fitted quantity is the cumulative mass. `kin` is in
  mass per cm^2 per hour.
- **Diclofenac units.** Figure 6D and Table 2 both give diclofenac in ug/cm^2
  (versus ng/cm^2 for the other three anti-inflammatory drugs), and the model
  follows them. Section 3.4 says diclofenac "penetrated in the lowest amount",
  which would hold only if those values were ng/cm^2. The parameters are
  unaffected by the unit label except that `kin` scales with it.
- **Species of the healthy-skin experiments.** Sections 2.4 and 2.6, the S2
  and S3 Fig captions and Table 2 (rat body-weight window) state rat skin for
  the temperature and anti-inflammatory experiments; Section 3.2 and the
  captions of Figures 4-6 say mouse skin. The models follow the Methods.
- **Figure label in S1 Table.** S1 Table labels the TNCB row as Figure
  "10.C"; Figure 10 has panels A and B only, and the TNCB curve is
  Figure 10B.
- **Model provenance citation.** Section 2.7 describes Eq 1 as a modified form
  of Eqs 55-57 of the paper's reference 1, which in the published reference
  list is a tacrolimus molecular-modelling study; the citation appears to be
  misnumbered. Eq 1 is printed in full, so the extraction does not depend on
  it.
- **Constant input.** `kin` is constant from time zero, i.e. the cream acts
  as an infinite-dose donor; the applied amount is not reported.
- No correction notice is linked to the article in Europe PMC as of
  2026-10-29.
